added_provisions.reason: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2(2)(a)-(b). The map treated the foreign-shareholding test as a one-off pre-completion check. Section 2(2) imposes a continuing condition: the company must keep foreign shareholding below fifty per cent for twenty consecutive years from the transfer, and if it reaches or exceeds fifty per cent the transfer becomes void from the date of the increase, subject to a six or twelve month cure window. Advising the purchasing company of that is part of the answer to 'what steps should you take'. Added as a supporting provision for M036-Q01.

Proviso to Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17). PROV-M036-015 states the search duty without its exception: the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, in which case he must instead endorse the reference to the previous registration before tendering the deed for registration. Added as a supporting provision for both questions and as an 'excepts' edge to PROV-M036-015.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (33). The most direct statutory anchor for calling in the vendor's title deed on a transfer: the notary must use his best endeavours to obtain the title deed and endorse the number, date and nature of the new transaction on it. M036-Q02 asks precisely what documents to call for and the map rested that limb only on rule (17) and the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance. Added as a supporting provision for both questions.

Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 32 of 2022 s.2(1). Supplies the caveat text actually in force at the matter date, which the corpus body of 23-1927/s32 (consolidated to 1990) does not carry. Added as a supporting provision for M036-Q02 and as an 'amends' edge to PROV-M036-025.

question_decisions.note: Every step in the gold answer traces to a provision in the corpus and the arithmetic checks out: 41 acres divided among five shareholders is 8.2 acres each against a fifty-acre ceiling, and Rs. 41,000,000 against an asset base of Rs. 60,000,000 exceeds half, so the acquisition is a major transaction. The two temporal soft spots (the as-enacted 'one hundred acres' in 2-1958/s25 and the 2024 consolidation of 7-1840/s2) were both handled correctly by the researcher and the outcome does not turn on either. Kept as proposed_gold; no indispensable provision was rejected or left unresolved. One rule claim (CL-M036-Q01-011) is marked disputed for over-narrowing Companies Act s.19(1)(a).

The document list is anchored provision by provision and the reasoning holds. The only defect found is temporal and does not touch an indispensable provision: PROV-M036-025 quotes the pre-2022 caveat text, now supplied in its in-force form by PROV-M036-904. Kept as proposed_gold. The gold answer's closing sentence about local-authority certificates is expressly disclaimed as outside the corpus and carries no answer claim, so it does not breach the citation rule, but a lawyer should decide whether it belongs in a gold answer at all.

disagreements.researcher_position: An obligation of the kind that a natural person must execute notarially 'is entered into on behalf of a company in writing signed under the company's name by two directors' (CL-M036-Q01-011, gold rule and application for M036-Q01).
disagreements.verifier_position: Companies Act s.19(1)(a) sets out four alternatives: two directors; the sole director if there is only one; any other person or class of persons if the articles so provide; or one or more attorneys appointed by the company. Stating the two-director route as the rule is an over-narrowing that an examiner could mark down. The claim should be reworded to give the alternatives, or the enrichment should state that the company has more than one director and no relevant article.

disagreements.disagreement_type: temporal text of a cited provision
disagreements.researcher_position: Registration of Documents Ordinance s.32 has no amendment event recorded against it and the 1927 text is applicable at the matter date (PROV-M036-025).
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 32(1) was repealed and substituted, and subsection (3) replaced with a two-year maximum, by the Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 32 of 2022 s.2, which was in force in October 2023. The corpus simply has no edge recording it. The substance the answer relies on survives, but the quoted text is not the in-force text and the 2022 version also carries new Form VIII, affidavit and attorney-at-law certificate requirements that a title examiner would need to know about.

disagreements.researcher_position: M036-Q01 and M036-Q02 are statute_only because the gold answers are deliberately confined to steps and documents that have a statutory anchor; local-authority certificates, physical inspection and the thirty-year root of title convention are recorded as corpus gaps and left out.
disagreements.verifier_position: That is defensible for the benchmark, but a marker of the original examination answer would expect the thirty-year root of title, physical inspection of the land and the local-authority certificates, none of which the corpus can supply. The questions remain statute_only on the evidence available, but the gold answers are narrower than a complete practitioner answer and a lawyer should decide whether they are scored as complete.

unsupported_claims: CL-M036-Q01-011 (disputed): Companies Act s.19(1)(a) does not require signature by two directors; it offers that as one of four alternatives.

CL-M036-Q01-014 (verified, inferential): the duty to obtain a registered discharge of the 2019 mortgage, or to redeem out of the purchase money, is an inference from the priority rule in 23-1927/s7(1) rather than its terms. Nothing in the corpus states it directly; the Mortgage Act No. 6 of 1949 was searched and yields no cleaner anchor.

M036-Q02 gold answer, closing sentence of the application: the call for local-authority certificates and rates receipts has no corpus anchor. It is expressly flagged as such in the prose and no answer claim rests on it.
temporal_issues: PROV-M036-025 / 23-1927/s32: corpus body is the pre-2022 text; s.32(1) was substituted by 32-2022 s.2(1), in force at the matter date. Corrected by adding PROV-M036-904 and downgrading PROV-M036-025 to partially_verified. The corpus records no amends edge for this, so the section's empty amendment_events list is misleading.

PROV-M036-001 / 2-1958/s25: corpus body is the as-enacted 'one hundred acres'. The extent limb in force at October 2023 reads 'twenty hectares' (20-2005 s.10(b) substituting for 'forty hectares', which is itself a metrication not carried in the corpus body). 41 acres is 16.6 hectares, below both thresholds, so the conclusion is unaffected; downgraded to partially_verified.

PROV-M036-013 / 7-1840/s2: correctly handled. The corpus body is consolidated to 2024 and its subsection (1)(a) and (2) carry Act No. 4 of 2024 text; the researcher cited the in-force October 2023 wording separately through 30-2022/s2 (PROV-M036-014). The 2024 transferee-signature rule is correctly excluded.

Notaries Ordinance s.31: Act No. 31 of 2022 and Act No. 6 of 2024 carry no separate date-of-operation clause in the corpus, so the 2022 rules ((6), (14), (16)(a), (17)(a), (17)(b)(i), (17)(d), (30A)) are in force at the matter date and the 2024 changes are not. The researcher's exclusion list is sound on the corpus evidence.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Proviso to Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17) (search may be dispensed with by written authority of the parties) - added as PROV-M036-902.
Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (33) (notary to use best endeavours to obtain the title deed) - added as PROV-M036-903, directly on point for M036-Q02.
Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2(2) (twenty-year maintenance of sub-fifty-per-cent foreign shareholding; transfer void on breach) - added as PROV-M036-901.

Land Reform Law s.3(3) (areas excluded from the acreage computation: half an acre round the residence, staff-quarter gardens, family burial ground) is not cited. It does not change the outcome here because the shareholders own no other agricultural land, so it was left out rather than added.

Land Reform Law s.42A onward (public companies) and Mortgage Act No. 6 of 1949 were both checked. The researcher's rejection of each holds: the purchaser is a private company, so s.8 is the operative route, and the Mortgage Act has no provision that states the discharge duty relied on in CL-M036-Q01-014 more directly than 23-1927/s7.
case_law_dependence: No case citation appears in either gold answer; the validator's case-law regex is clean. The prescriptive-possession limb of M036-Q02 is anchored on Prescription Ordinance s.3 rather than on judicial authority, and the bona fide purchaser and thirty-year root points were kept out.
enrichment_issues: M036-Q01 FACT-M036-Q01-004 states the extent in hectares (16.6) and says the estate 'has never been registered, and is not deemed to be registered, as an estate in the statutory register of rubber estates'. That tracks the two limbs of the s.25 definition closely enough to telegraph the analysis, and the hectare figure hints at the metric threshold. No statute name or section number is disclosed, so it does not breach the leak rule, but a lawyer may want it stated more neutrally.
M036-Q01 FACT-M036-Q01-003 says the articles 'contain no provision expressly authorising the acquisition of estate property', echoing the wording of Companies Act s.185(1)(d). Same observation.
M036-Q01 FACT-M036-Q01-001 says no share is held 'directly or indirectly' by any person outside Sri Lanka, echoing s.2(1)(b). Same observation.

All six M036-Q01 facts and all six M036-Q02 facts carry a reason and a counterfactual, and each synthetic_decisive fact does explain why it is needed. None changes the legal issue posed by the original question, and none states the conclusion.
The Rs. 41,000,000 figure used in FACT-M036-Q01-003 comes from part 3 of the same past-paper question (M036-Q03, Tier B, not in this map), so it is not an invented value inconsistent with the source.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: PROV-M036-010 and PROV-M036-011 are two subsections of the same section (7-2007/s185) carried as separate provisions; that is deliberate and correct, since (1) supplies the prohibition and (2) the definition.

PROV-M036-015 through PROV-M036-021, and the added PROV-M036-902 and PROV-M036-903, all sit on 1-1907/s31. Nine provision entries against one section id is heavy, but each carries a distinct rule and a distinct verbatim excerpt.

M036-Q01 and M036-Q02 share ten provisions. The questions are genuinely different (steps on a purchase versus documents on a title examination) and the enriched backgrounds concern two different parcels and two different vendors, so this is overlap rather than duplication.

lawyer_questions: Companies Act s.19(1)(a) gives four ways a company may execute a notarially attested obligation. Should the gold answer for M036-Q01 state all four, or should the enrichment be tightened (for example, that the company has two or more directors and no relevant article) so that the two-director route is the only correct one? This is the one substantive correction the verifier would make to the gold prose.

The caveat provision quoted at PROV-M036-025 is the 1927 text; the text in force in October 2023 is the substituted section 32(1) (added as PROV-M036-904), which restricts caveators to persons with or claiming a right, title or interest and imposes Form VIII, an affidavit and an attorney-at-law certificate. Should the gold answer for M036-Q02 be scored against the 2022 text?

The Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act extent threshold in the corpus is the as-enacted 'one hundred acres'; the in-force threshold is 'twenty hectares'. The 41-acre estate is below both, so nothing turns on it here, but should the corpus edition be refreshed before other rubber or tea estate matters are annotated?

Are M036-Q01 and M036-Q02 acceptable as statute_only when the gold answers deliberately omit the thirty-year root of title, physical inspection and local-authority certificates that a marker would expect?
